implementation: RP2040-only32-bit tiny-integer decode/pack, standard pointer+hint ABI to existing independent midpoint checks, and a specialized exact-normalized128-bit square. Source-rewrite/mask proofs retain all previous rounding, domain and error acceptance rules. Every declined untrusted seed retains the identical previous refinement path.

source_certificate.candidate_route: Only the normal-cell ambiguous exit changes. The rounded Q62 value is an untrusted hint. The existing dyadic midpoint inequalities retain authority; all overlap/domain declines use the identical previous refinement function. The synchronous call receives pointers to live double parameters and does not retain or modify them.
source_certificate.square_identity: Three exact32x32->64 products reconstruct the full64-bit square by the displayed radix identity and middle carry. The normalized128-bit square uses the same two equal cross-high terms and the identical propagated radius as the generic aliased product. This preserves the full output triple byte-for-byte; independent ARM tests check all carry/normalization cases.
source_certificate.scope: Exact source-rewrite equivalence and square carry bounds. The bounded tiny-helper bit-mask proof is separate. Compiled pointer ABI, exact square/enclosure results, RNE and M4/generic isolation require their independent ARM/compiler checks. No universal pow totality, cache policy or physical-speed proof.

tiny32_certificate.proof: For exponent0..16, the old36..52-bit integer mask decomposes exactly into the whole low32 word and a4..20-bit mask of the21-bit high significand. Quotient shifts and n<=65536 are identical. The same exact64-bit product is tested; accepting a nonzero high32 word is impossible under the old threshold. Every accepted units/units+1/shifted-units value fits32bits. The reconstructed64-bit output expressions are therefore identical, with the same decline behavior and unchanged binomial remainder argument.
tiny32_certificate.scope: Algebraic bit-mask and width identities for the RP2040 specialization. ARM baseline comparison and MPFR tests separately check compiled code. Non-RP2040 code keeps the old implementation. No physical-speed or universal pow-totality claim.

integer_certificate.multiplication_identity: AB/2^128=aH*bH+(aL*bH+aH*bL)/2^64+aL*bL/2^128. The retained exact high products omit a positive tail<3. Input radii contribute <Ea+Eb+1; the code uses4, or smaller certified zero-low-word cases. Normalization scales the radius by at most2.
integer_certificate.reciprocal_and_dyadic_acceptance: For positive x and midpoint m, sign(x^(p/q)-m)=sign(x^p-m^q); for a negative exponent it equals-sign(x^p*m^q-1). Only strict disjoint integer enclosures decide a side. Two adjacent strict midpoint sides certify a unique RNE cell, independently of the seed. Exact ties and overlapping enclosures decline to the existing path.
integer_certificate.scope: Exact rational tail/error inequalities, all discrete exponentiation-chain bounds, shift-alignment and exponent-width bounds. Source hashes bind the inspected algorithms. Independent ARM interval/MPFR tests must check compiled arithmetic and control-flow integration. No universal pow totality or physical-speed proof.
integer_certificate.exact_sqrt_cube_lemma: A proposed positive binary64 root has an exact106-bit square in the normalized128-bit format. Equal exponent/significand and zero low/error certify root^2=x exactly. Thus x^(3/2)=x*root and one existing IEEE binary64 multiplication supplies RNE, including exact midpoint parity; no rounded-square equality is used.

square_arm.scope: Every actual ARM square result, radius and exponent equals the qualified generic aliased product byte-for-byte and independently encloses both exact rational input endpoints squared. All-bit carry boundaries, maximal words, zero low words, random full128-bit mantissas and nonzero input radii are included. Every call checks ABI and stack writes. Finite coverage plus the source algebraic identity; not hardware cycles or general pow totality.

candidate_arm.scope: Actual ARM pointer+hint entry, with identical, adjacent, distant, random and invalid seeds, including aliased parameter pointers. Every direct return and selected public return matches directed MPFR; parameter bytes and surrounding canaries remain unchanged. Captured ROM executes and every call checks callee-saved registers, SP and stack writes. Finite ABI/fallback coverage, not an all-input precision or physical-speed proof.

tiny_integer_arm.scope: Actual compiled tiny-integer helper against the qualified parent, including exact canary preservation on declines. All accepted results independently match directed MPFR. Integer/exponent/caller-distance boundaries, threshold crossings, both signs and fractional/NaN/infinite declines are included. Public integration calls verify returned RNE values. This is finite coverage supplementing the bit-mask equivalence proof, not hardware-cycle or general-totality evidence.

dyadic_arm.scope: Actual production ARM dyadic midpoint decisions checked with independently formed exact rational x^p and midpoint^q, including jittered valid input enclosures. Both exponent signs and denominator powers through128 are covered. Exact, adjacent, distant and invalid hints have no rounding authority; every accepted result matches directed MPFR. Selected full public calls check integration. This is finite coverage, not totality or physical-speed proof.

all12.oracle: Directed MPFR bounds; both endpoints round to the same binary64 (RNE).
all12.abi: Every call verifies R4-R11, SP, bounded stack writes.
all12.semantics: RNE return values; errno and floating exception flags are not implemented.
all12.nan_result_policy: NaN results must be quiet; payload and sign are unspecified.
known_limitations: An undecided owned 1024-bit pow refinement still traps; all-input totality is unproved.
all12.scope: Finite corpus, not an exhaustive proof over every binary64 input.

instruction_matrix.scope: Executed ARM instructions on the prepared finite corpus, with typed 32-bit return masking. If sides_share_elf is false, owned production symbols and pinned diagnostic Qfplib symbols run on separate instances of the same Cortex-M0 emulator. When actual_bootrom is present, SDK ROM lookup initializers, wrappers and ROM bodies execute without intrinsic models. SIO division remains functionally modeled. These are not hardware cycles, cache comparisons, timings, or proof of speed parity.

hard_profile.scope: Seeded reservoir of published hard pow inputs in three explicit finite domains. Positive normal bases and bounded logarithm-products keep the composed Qfplib ln/mul/exp comparison meaningful. Actual production/diagnostic ARM and captured ROM execute on separate identical emulator instances. Instruction counts are not physical cycles or timings. This is additional coverage, not a replacement for the 114-group matrix or an all-input proof.

affected_corpus.oracle: Directed MPFR bounds must round to the same binary64; signaling NaNs separately require a quiet NaN result.
affected_corpus.abi: Every ARM call verifies R4-R11, SP and bounded stack writes.
affected_corpus.scope: Saved worst-case corpus; not a totality proof over all binary64 pairs.
known_limitations: The owned 512/1024-bit fallback preserves a final undecided-interval trap; totality is unproved.

affected_selector.selection: Union of all saved entries with |y|=p/q, p<=32 and q<=128, and all new tiny-binomial dispatch gates. Selection places no restriction on base encodings and includes both exponent signs. These cover every potentially accepted new numerical path in the saved corpus; unsupported cases provably decline and remain on existing paths. Line ranges refer to the unchanged full corpus.
affected_selector.scope: Deterministic exact binary64 exponent-domain selection, not numerical qualification. The complete resulting subset must independently pass the ARM/MPFR runner.

resources_and_link.scope: Only the bounded tiny helper, normal first-tier candidate route and exact square kernel/callers change numerical code. The unchanged integer boundary helper also changes literal-pool alignment by2bytes. Other prior native functions retain identical object bytes; four other numeric objects including allocated relocations are identical. Three unchanged RAM shift routines move24bytes; other non-pow linked functions retain addresses and have identical bytes or calls/veneers to equivalent targets. Main-RAM boundaries and4096-byte scratch reservation are unchanged; actual scratch use is4088bytes with one new canonical16-byte candidate veneer. Physical XIP/cycle effects are not established by this link check.

M4_isolation.scope: Cortex-M4 O3 release, both soft and hard float ABIs: normalized preprocessing and every allocated code/data section identical; existing M4 runtime sources byte-identical

generic_M0_isolation.scope: Non-RP2040 generic ARMv6-M: every allocated code/data section remains byte-identical to V60. The generic spelling has an extra expression macro; normalized preprocessing identity is not claimed.

cache_probe.assumptions: Same previously checked 16 KiB / two-way / 8-byte-line cache geometry; LRU/FIFO replacement and whole-line/per-word fills are explicit model assumptions. These are not claims about undocumented prefetch or replacement.
cache_probe.scope: Exact ARM instruction/data traces and exact results on the recorded finite groups per image, including every ln/log10 stream and the three difficult pow streams, with actual ROM and linked memory code. Two warm passes then a measured third pass. Only XIP accesses enter the cache model. Excludes caller prefetch, IRQs, other-core traffic and Qfplib batches. Not measured XIP counters or physical speed evidence.

prior_million_run_scope: The complete1,003,177-case run belongs to V86, not V98. V98 separately passes the full75,229-entry subset covering every potentially newly accepted pow path in that unchanged corpus, plus targeted tiny-helper equivalence tests and poisoned-seed ABI tests. Source and object/relocation proofs cover unchanged paths. Finite tests do not establish universal totality.
cache_scope: Actual instruction/data traces, four explicit warmed models: only the two hard streams change misses, both improving; the other17 streams match. No hardware counters, physical cache policy, caller prefetch, IRQ or other-core traffic is measured.
